parts.role: Power in from the DC jack, through F1 and SW1: pin 1 is +12 V, pin 2 is 0 V.

parts.orientation: Band (cathode) toward the +12 V row, row 2. Stands upright.
parts.role: Reverse-polarity shunt: if the supply is connected backwards it conducts and blows F1, so nothing else is damaged. Normally it does nothing.
parts.note: Legs ~1.3 mm: open the holes up. A 1N4007 also works.

parts.orientation: Stripe (−) toward the 0 V row, row 4. Stands upright.
parts.role: Bulk smoothing on the +12 V input. With C1B in parallel it makes 200 µF.

parts.orientation: Stripe (−) toward the 0 V row, row 4. Stands upright.
parts.role: Bulk smoothing on the +12 V input, in parallel with C1A.
Steps the 12 V supply down to the 5 V the chip, the LCD and the LEDs run on.
parts.note: Sits on double-sided foam tape with four short wires to the rails; keep its 22 × 17 mm outline clear. Read the module's own silkscreen for IN+, IN−, OUT+ and OUT−. An LM2596 module, or a 7805 with a heatsink, also works.

parts.orientation: Stripe (−) toward the 0 V row, row 4.
parts.role: Smoothing on U1's 5 V output.
Fast decoupling on +5 V right next to U1.

parts.orientation: Stripe (−) toward the 0 V row, row 4.
parts.role: Extra smoothing on the +5 V rail.

parts.orientation: Pin 1 (0 V) at column 20, on the left.
parts.role: Fan A: pin 1 is 0 V, pin 2 +12 V, pin 3 the speed (tach) signal, pin 4 PWM.

parts.orientation: Pin 1 (0 V) at column 26, on the left.
parts.role: Fan B: pin 1 is 0 V, pin 2 +12 V, pin 3 the speed (tach) signal, pin 4 PWM.
Pull-up on the chip's reset pin (U2 pin 1), so the chip runs instead of staying in reset.
The controller: reads both fans' speed, drives the PWM, the two status LEDs and the LCD, and reads the speed knob.
parts.note: Solder the socket, not the chip. Plug the chip in only after the power-up checks (Build Guide §7).

parts.role: Decoupling for the chip's supply, VCC and GND on pins 7 and 8.
parts.note: Mounted underneath, across socket pins 7–8, to keep its legs short.

parts.role: Steadies AREF (pin 21), the reference the chip measures the speed knob against.
Decoupling for AVCC (pin 20), the supply of the chip's analogue part.
parts.note: Mounted underneath, from pin 20 to the 0 V spur hole directly above it.

parts.role: The chip's 16 MHz clock, on pins 9 and 10.
parts.note: Mounted underneath, across pins 9–10, legs bent inward.

parts.role: Load capacitor for the crystal, pin 9 to 0 V. Without it the clock may not start.
Load capacitor for the crystal, pin 10 to 0 V.
Pull-up on fan A's speed (tach) line to +5 V. The fan's tach output can only pull low.
Carries fan A's speed signal into the chip (pin 4), and protects the pin if a fan lead ever touches +12 V.
Pull-up on fan B's speed (tach) line to +5 V.
Carries fan B's speed signal into the chip (pin 5), and protects the pin if a fan lead ever touches +12 V.
Pull-up on the shared PWM line to +5 V. With Q1 off, the fans see 100 %.
Base resistor from the chip's PWM pin (pin 15, D9) to Q1, so the pin isn't overloaded.

parts.orientation: Flat face toward row 16 (down). E, B, C left to right: check the pinout of your part (Build Guide §6).
parts.role: Switches both fans' PWM line low under the chip's control, so one pin drives both fans.
Holds Q1 off, so the fans run at 100 % if the controller is dead or in reset (fail-safe).
Current limit for status LED D2 (fan A), from pin 11.
Current limit for status LED D3 (fan B), from pin 12.
Smooths the speed knob's voltage into pin 23 (A0), so the reading doesn't jitter.
To the front panel: pin 1 +5 V, 2 knob wiper, 3 0 V, 4 LED A, 5 LED B, 6 0 V.
To the LCD's I²C backpack: pin 1 0 V, 2 +5 V, 3 SDA, 4 SCL.
To push-button SW2: pin 1 to the chip's pin 6 (D4), pin 2 to 0 V.
The fan-speed knob on the front panel, read on pin 23.
parts.note: Off the board, wired to J5. If the knob turns the wrong way, swap its two outer wires.

parts.orientation: Long leg (anode) to R2 through J5; short leg (cathode, flat side) to 0 V.
parts.role: Fan A status light.

parts.orientation: Long leg (anode) to R3 through J5; short leg (cathode, flat side) to 0 V.
parts.role: Fan B status light.

parts.value: 1 A fitted for now; 2 A slow-blow with the USB port
parts.role: Protects the wiring against a short, and is what D1 blows if the supply is connected backwards.
parts.note: In a panel holder, between the DC jack and SW1. 1 A is fine without the USB port (0.67 A steady); fit the 2 A slow-blow when you build sheet 3.

parts.role: Main power switch.
parts.note: Panel cutout 19.2 × 13 mm. The lamp terminal goes to 0 V.
